canonical_name: LOFT (Long-Context Frontiers; Lee et al., Google DeepMind) - 'Can Long-Context Language Models Subsume Retrieval, RAG, SQL, and More?'
release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.13121 (v1 2024-06-19); repo initial data release 2024-06-20 https://github.com/google-deepmind/loft
metric: per-dataset primary metric (recall@1 / mrecall@k for retrieval, subspan EM for RAG, accuracy for SQL & many-shot ICL), averaged; headline used here = LOFT-hard retrieval average (MuSiQue, QAMPARI, QUEST) at <=128K context, as reported by the creator lab (Google)
abandoned_evidence: Last lab report 2025-06-17 (Gemini 2.5 technical report, LOFT hard retrieval <=128K / 1M); no report by the 9 labs found afterwards (Gemini 3/3.1 cards use MRCR v2 instead); no official leaderboard exists; last commit to github.com/google-deepmind/loft on 2025-06-13. >15 months of inactivity by cutoff.
score_at_release: 75.9 (LOFT-hard <=128K value for Gemini 1.5 Pro as later reported in the Gemini 2.5 report); the 2024-06 paper gives only per-task 128k averages: text retrieval 0.77, visual retrieval 0.83, audio retrieval 1.00, RAG 0.53, SQL 0.38, many-shot ICL 0.68 (Claude 3 Opus 0.74)
n_items: 35 datasets x up to 100 test queries per dataset per context length (32k/128k/1M); LOFT-hard = 3 datasets (~300 queries)
modality: text (headline LOFT-hard); full LOFT also image, video, audio retrieval
lineage: arXiv 2406.13121 (2024-06) -> published as 'LOFT: Scalable and More Realistic Long-Context Evaluation' (Findings of NAACL 2025); README defines LOFT-hard subset (MuSiQue, QAMPARI, QUEST) recommended for iteration; QUEST-LOFT-128K-Revised relabel by Google DeepMind authors (arXiv 2511.06125, 2025-11). Google later shifted long-context reporting to MRCR v2.
best_by_cutoff: 87.0 - Gemini 2.5 Pro, LOFT (hard retrieval) <=128K, Gemini 2.5 technical report 2025-06-17 (arXiv 2507.06261 Table 3); same report 1M: 69.8. Other: Grok 3 Beta 83.3 on 'LOFT (128k)' averaged across 12 tasks (x.ai/news/grok-3, 2025-02-19).
notes: No human baseline -> criterion B (90). No result >=90 found on any LOFT aggregate by cutoff. Context-length choice: <=128K is the headline variant used by both reporting labs (Google 'hard retrieval <=128K', xAI '128k'); 1M results much lower (Gemini 2.5 Pro 69.8). xAI's 83.3 is a different, undocumented 12-task aggregation (not comparable with LOFT-hard). Independent audit (arXiv 2511.06125, Google DeepMind authors, 2025-11) found that 'a third or more of the errors' on QUEST-LOFT-128K were cases where the gold answer was incorrect or debatable - affects one of the 3 LOFT-hard datasets; does not meet E(iii) (no >=20% defect share of whole benchmark quantified and no lab publicly stopped reporting because of it). Abandonment judged on lab reports + repo activity since there is no leaderboard. Lab reports list taken from input; a quick search found no later lab reports.

canonical_name: LifeSciBench (OpenAI) - 'Evaluating Language Models on Realistic ... Life-Science Research' (750 expert-authored tasks, rubric-graded)
release_source: https://openai.com/index/introducing-life-sci-bench/ (2026-06-17); preprint https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/b4299379-0a97-4ffa-8b9b-c3fbb299caa9/lifescibench_preprint.pdf ; earlier mention in GPT-Rosalind post 2026-06-03 per input lab report (not independently verified)
metric: mean normalized rubric score (0-100%) and task pass rate (share of tasks with >=70% of rubric met); OpenAI release posts after launch report a single % that matches the normalized-score scale
lineage: New benchmark (2026-06); related OpenAI rubric benchmarks HealthBench (2025-05). No successor by cutoff.
best_by_cutoff: 60.3 - GPT-6 Astra, OpenAI release post (https://openai.com/index/gpt-6-astra/, 2026-09); GPT-5.6 Sol 59.9 (2026-07-09). Metric appears to be normalized rubric score; best known pass rate 36.1 (GPT-Rosalind, 2026-06-17).
notes: Borderline stratum: publicly documented (announcement + preprint with results on Google/xAI models; 'Request access' / 'Join as a contributor'), but tasks/rubrics are not openly released by cutoff (preprint: 'Public release of tasks, rubrics, artifacts, or evaluation materials may be limited by licensing, privacy, proprietary information, or biological safety considerations'; llm-stats page: 'Dataset Soon'). Coded main with test_access=private-heldout; a strict reading of 'no public items' would make it excluded:internal. Only OpenAI reports it (3 releases). No human performance baseline (453 expert reviewers validated tasks but did not solve them) -> criterion B. Grader model for rubric scoring not named in sources read; class=LLM-judge assumed from rubric-graded free-form format. Date discrepancy: input lists GPT-6 Astra report 2026-09-03; WebFetch of openai.com/index/gpt-6-astra/ returned 'September 22, 2026' - either way before cutoff. Far from threshold (best ~60%).

canonical_name: LiveBench: A Challenging, Contamination-Free LLM Benchmark (White et al.; Abacus.AI/NYU et al.)
release_source: https://github.com/LiveBench/LiveBench/blob/main/changelog.md ('2024-06-12 Introducing LiveBench ... we release the initial batch of 960 questions'); paper https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.19314 (v1 2024-06-27)

n_items: 960 at launch (2024-06-12); held at ~1,000 questions from 2024-07-26 with rolling replacement; newest questions withheld from public HF release for a period
lineage: Rolling releases (leaderboard data files): 2024-06-24, 2024-07-26, 2024-08-31, 2024-11-25, 2025-04-02, 2025-04-25 (coding no longer from LiveCodeBench), 2025-05-30 (agentic coding category; agent switched to mini-SWE-agent 2025-10-03), 2025-11-25 (refresh 'to resolve (to some extent) saturation and contamination'), 2025-12-23, 2026-01-08, 2026-06-25 (agentic v2). Coding questions drew on LiveCodeBench until 2025-04.
best_by_cutoff: 82.4 Global Average - gemini-2.5-pro-exp-03-25 on release 2024-11-25 (added to leaderboard 2025-03-27; max over full git history of github.com/LiveBench/livebench.github.io tables, computed as mean of category means). On latest release 2026-06-25: gpt-5.5-xhigh 79.9 (leaderboard commit 2026-07-06); on 2026-01-08 release gpt-5.5-xhigh 80.7 (2026-04-23). Best lab self-report: Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507 78.4 (LiveBench 2024-11-25, 2025-07-25).
notes: Rolling benchmark: per codebook only C or E can end it; AB recorded for information only - no release ever had a Global Average >=90 (max 82.35). No C event: maintainers keep releasing (2026-06-25 release; main repo commits through 2026-09-29); task-level refreshes citing saturation (2024-11-25: 'increasing the difficulty of tasks for which o1 ... achieved very high scores'; 2025-11-25: 'to resolve (to some extent) saturation and contamination') are part of the rolling design, not closure/replacement of the benchmark. Earlier task removal 2024-06-24 (house traversal) for parsing ambiguity. No independent compromise evidence (E) found. Lab reports stopped after 2025-10-30 (Kimi Linear) but leaderboard remains active, so not abandoned. Lab self-reports use frozen older releases (e.g., '2024-11-25'); o3-mini 'LiveBench Coding' 84.6 is a category score, not overall. Website leaderboard repo last updated 2026-07-06 (no GPT-5.6/GPT-6 entries yet as of cutoff).

lineage: Rolling releases on HF livecodebench/code_generation_lite: v1 (2024-04), v2 (2024-06-02), v3 (2024-08-12), v4 (2024-10-06), v5 (2025-01-14), v6 (2025-04-21); no data release after v6 (last HF commit 2025-06-05 typo fix). LCB site added GSO leaderboard page 2025-06-12 (no replacement statement).
best_by_cutoff: Lab self-report: 93.5 DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Max (LiveCodeBench Pass@1, v6 per input), HF model card 2026-04-24 https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro (same table: Gemini-3.1-Pro High 91.7, Kimi K2.6 Thinking 89.6); Qwen3.7-Max 91.6 (2026-05-20). Official leaderboard (last update 2025-08-01): o4-mini (High) 84.7 on default window 2023-12-01..2025-05-01 (769 problems), 75.8 on 2025-01..2025-05.
notes: Rolling benchmark: per codebook only C or E can end it; AB recorded for information only. No C: no public closure/deprecation statement found, but updates stopped silently (last dataset release v6 2025-04-21; leaderboard repo last commit 2025-08-01 'add new results'; main repo last commit 2025-07-16). Labs keep self-reporting on frozen v5/v6 windows through 2026-06; first lab self-report >=90 = DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Max 93.5 (2026-04-24) - would be an AB event (2026-04) if the unit were treated as a static/frozen benchmark after updates stopped; flag for sensitivity analysis. Not abandoned (lab reports continue until 2026-06-01). ERRATA.md lists ~17 problematic problems (multiple valid outputs, 2 interactive, a few erroneous tests) out of 1,055 (<20%) -> no E. Window heterogeneity across lab reports makes scores not strictly comparable (e.g., Gemini uses 1/1/2025-5/1/2025, DeepSeek 2408-2505).

exclusion_reason: Primary/leaderboard metric is an Elo-based Rating (Bayesian MAP Elo vs. human Codeforces contestants, open-ended Codeforces scale); the paper's main leaderboard is ranked by Rating and Google reports only Elo (2439/2316/2887).

canonical_name: LongBench (v1): A Bilingual, Multitask Benchmark for Long Context Understanding (Bai et al., THUDM; ACL 2024) - NOTE: input raw_names are other benchmarks (MMLongBench-Doc, LongBench-Chat), see notes
release_source: https://huggingface.co/datasets/THUDM/LongBench (data.zip uploaded 2023-08-01; repo commits from 2023-07-29 https://github.com/THUDM/LongBench); paper https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.14508 (2023-08-28)
metric: average of task metrics (F1 for QA, ROUGE-L for summarization, accuracy for classification/synthetic, edit similarity for code) over 21 datasets / 6 categories, 0-100 (reported for EN, ZH, overall)
abandoned_evidence: No report of LongBench v1 by the 9 labs in the input (the 3 'LongBench' lab rows are LongBench-Chat and MMLongBench-Doc). Official README leaderboard last gained a model on 2023-10-30 (ChatGLM3-6B-32k); v1 files demoted to LongBench/ subfolder when LongBench v2 launched (2024-12-18/20). >12 months inactivity before cutoff.
n_items: 4,750 test instances, 21 datasets (14 EN, 5 ZH, 2 code); plus LongBench-E length-balanced subset
lineage: LongBench v1 (2023-08) -> LongBench v2 (2024-12-20, 503 MCQ; repo README: 'Compared to the first generation of LongBench, LongBench v2 is much longer and much more challenging'); sibling THUDM benchmark LongBench-Chat (LongAlign, arXiv 2401.18058, 2024-01-31). Unrelated: MMLongBench-Doc (Ma et al., arXiv 2407.01523, 2024-07-01).
best_by_cutoff: Not established from primary sources: official leaderboard frozen at 2023-10 (top EN avg 44.0 GPT-3.5-Turbo-16k among listed models); no source found reporting a LongBench v1 average anywhere near 90 (ROUGE-L/F1 metrics cap aggregate scores far below the scale maximum).
notes: LIKELY GROUPING ERROR IN INPUT: the 3 lab reports under 'LongBench' are (a) LongBench-Chat (Qwen2.5 TR 2024-12-19, score 8.72 on a 1-10 GPT-4-judged scale; THUDM, LongAlign 2024-01) and (b) MMLongBench-Doc (Qwen3.5 61.5, 2026-02-16; Qwen3.6-Plus 62.0, 2026-04-01; multimodal long-document benchmark, 1,062 questions/130 PDFs, arXiv 2407.01523, 2024-07-01; best at release GPT-4o F1 42.7). Neither alone meets the population rule from the input (MMLongBench-Doc: one lab, 2 releases; LongBench-Chat: 1 release), and LongBench v1 itself has no lab report in the input -> recommend the coordinator drop or re-split this unit. Coded here as LongBench v1 per the unit name. No C: LongBench v2 paper criticizes earlier benchmarks ('adopted metrics like F1 and ROUGE are unreliable', extractive/synthetic tasks) but does not deprecate v1 or cite saturation. Independent critique arXiv 2505.19293 (2025-05) questions whether LongBench measures long-context ability - does not meet E (no near-ceiling trivial method). Release month: repo/HF commits 2023-07-29..31 but data.zip upload 2023-08-01 and paper 2023-08-28 -> 2023-08 (2023-07 defensible).

score_at_release_system: o1-preview (w/ CoT); best direct-answer GPT-4o 50.1; human experts 53.7
lineage: Successor of LongBench v1 (2023-08) by the same THUDM group; v1 files moved to LongBench/ subfolder at v2 launch.
best_by_cutoff: 69.1 - Claude Opus 4.8 as evaluated by Qwen in the Qwen3.8-Max model card (https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-FP8, 2026-08; same table GPT-5.6 Sol max 67.1, Qwen3.8-Max 66.3, Qwen3.7-Max 65.3). Official leaderboard (longbench2.github.io, last commit 2025-08-30): Gemini-2.5-Pro 63.3 w/ CoT.

Leaderboard repo inactive since 2025-08-30 but labs still report (Qwen 2026-08-03, DeepSeek base-model 2026-09-10), so not abandoned. DeepSeek reports a base-model 1-shot EM variant (51.5 / 45.2) - different protocol. Opus 4.8's 69.1 is a third-party (Qwen) evaluation, not an Anthropic self-report.

canonical_name: MATH: Measuring Mathematical Problem Solving With the MATH Dataset (Hendrycks et al., 2021) - full 5,000-problem test set
metric: accuracy (exact match of final boxed answer after normalization)
ab_mode: best-of-256 with reward-model selection (rm@256); same model 80.6 with a single sample
ab_source: Gemini 1.5 technical report update 2024-05-17 (https://storage.googleapis.com/deepmind-media/gemini/gemini_v1_5_report.pdf ; arXiv 2403.05530 v3 2024-06-14): 'accuracy of 80.6% on the MATH benchmark from a single sample, and an accuracy of 91.1% when sampling 256 solutions and selecting a candidate answer (rm@256)' (quoted in wccftech 2024-05-20); Sundar Pichai on X 2024-05-17: 'MATH benchmark for specialized version now at 91.1%'
score_at_release_system: GPT-2 1.5B pretrained on AMPS then fine-tuned on MATH (GPT-3 175B few-shot 5.2)
lineage: Companion AMPS pretraining corpus; official IID subset MATH-500 (Lightman et al., 'Let's Verify Step by Step', 2023-05; 4,500 of the other test problems used in PRM800K training); variants Functional MATH (2024-02), MATH Level 5 (HF Open LLM Leaderboard v2, 2024-06), MATH-Perturb (2025). OpenAI simple-evals switched to MATH-500 for o1 and later models (2024-09).
best_by_cutoff: No-tool results on the full set: 91.1 Gemini 1.5 Pro math-specialized rm@256 (2024-05); single-sample self-report Gemini 2.0 Flash 90.9 (Google model card 2025-02-05, per input). Labs largely moved to MATH-500 (97-98%) from late 2024; later full-MATH reports are base-model few-shot runs (e.g., Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-Base 74.1).
notes: Human data in paper: 3 university students, 20 problems each, 1 hour, by hand: 40% (dislikes math), 90% (AMC 10 perfect score / USAMO), 90% (three-time IMO gold medalist); mean 73.3 -> criterion B (90). Treating the two strong participants (90%) as an expert baseline would give A with the same threshold 90, so the event date is unaffected. AB counted under main mode because best-of-N with a reward-model verifier is allowed; no-tool. Earlier higher-looking results used code execution (GPT-4 Code Interpreter CSV 84.3, 2023-08; MACM w/ code 87.9, 2024) and do not count. Caution on input lab rows: OpenAI 'MATH' scores for o1-preview 85.5, o1-2024-12-17 96.4, o3-mini 97.9 are MATH-500 (simple-evals footnote: 'For newer models (anything on or after o1) we evaluate on MATH-500') - assigned to the MATH-500 unit. First single-model pass@1 self-report >=90 on full MATH: Gemini 2.0 Flash 90.9 (2025-02) (Gemini 2.0 Flash Exp 89.7, 2024-12). Strict event not established: independent evaluators use subsets (MATH-500, MATH Level 5, HELM subsample) rather than the full 5,000 problems. No C/E: contamination concerns (public AoPS solutions; Functional MATH 'reasoning gap' 2024-02) do not meet E(i) as specified. Could not read the Gemini 1.5 report text directly (PDF truncated in fetch); quote taken from contemporaneous coverage.

canonical_name: MATH-500 (500-problem IID held-out subset of the MATH test set; Lightman et al., OpenAI, 'Let's Verify Step by Step')
metric: accuracy (exact match of final answer), pass@1
ab_system: OpenAI o1 (pre-release 'work in progress' o1); same day o1-mini 90.0 (released)
ab_source: https://openai.com/index/learning-to-reason-with-llms/ (2024-09-12; 'Our evaluations used the same 500 problem test split found in' Lightman et al.); simple-evals README commit fb3f1ef 2024-09-11 (o1 94.8, o1-mini 90.0, o1-preview 85.5; footnote 'For o1 models, we evaluate on MATH-500')
strict_source: Hugging Face open-r1 independent reproduction with lighteval, README commit bd0e15b 2025-01-30 https://github.com/huggingface/open-r1 (upper bound: Artificial Analysis Quality Index already included independently-run MATH-500 by 2024-12-16, per AA 2024 review, but per-model scores/dates not retrievable)
score_at_release_system: GPT-4-based generator + process reward model (PRM), best-of-1860
lineage: Subset of MATH (Hendrycks et al., 2021-03); created because 4,500 MATH test problems were used to train PRM800K models. Became the de facto MATH protocol for reasoning models from 2024-09 (OpenAI simple-evals; DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, Anthropic, Meta, Mistral). Labs moved on to AIME-style evals in 2025.
best_by_cutoff: 98.2 - o4-mini-high, OpenAI simple-evals README (commit 2025-04-14; o3-high 98.1); Qwen3-235B-A22B thinking 98.0 (Qwen3 tech report 2025-05-14).
notes: No human baseline for the subset -> criterion B (90). AB = first public >=90: OpenAI 2024-09-12 o1 94.8 / o1-mini 90.0 (pass@1). No earlier >=90 on MATH-500 found (mid-2024 PRM/MCTS papers on MATH-500 were far lower; Gemini 1.5 Pro math-specialized 91.1 rm@256 (2024-05) was on the full MATH set). OpenAI 'MATH' numbers for o1 and later models (o1-preview 85.5, o1-1217 96.4, o3-mini 97.9) are MATH-500 per simple-evals footnote - the input lists some of them under MATH. Strict event uses an independent reproduction (HF open-r1) - an upper bound; earlier independent runs >=90 (Artificial Analysis, from ~2024-Q4) likely exist. No C/E found; simple-evals deprecation notice (2025-07: 'will no longer be updated for new models or benchmark results') concerns the repo, not the dataset.

canonical_name: MAWPS: A Math Word Problem Repository (Koncel-Kedziorski et al., NAACL 2016)
metric: answer accuracy; supervised-solver protocol = 5-fold cross-validation on the 1,987/2,373-problem single-equation subset; LLM-era reports use differing subset combinations (AddSub, SingleEq, SingleOp, MultiArith)
ab_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.10316 (2022-03-19); ACL 2022 https://aclanthology.org/2022.acl-long.410.pdf (MAWPS: BERT-DeductReasoner 91.2, RoBERTa-DeductReasoner 92.0; prior best Roberta-Graph2Tree 88.7)
score_at_release_system: Koncel-Kedziorski et al. (2015) equation-tree solver on SingleEq; Kushman et al. (2014) 68.7 on SimulEq-S (MAWPS paper reports per-subset baselines only)
n_items: 3,320 problems at publication with an official 80/20 train/test split; common ML protocol: 5-fold CV on 1,987 (Jie et al.) / 2,373 single-unknown problems
lineage: Aggregates earlier datasets (AddSub 2014, SingleOp, SingleEq 2015, MultiArith 2015, SimulEq/ALG514 2014); related successors ASDiv (2020), SVAMP (2021, built from ASDiv-A/MAWPS-style problems to expose shallow heuristics), GSM8K (2021).
best_by_cutoff: Not established as a single comparable number (protocols differ). Supervised: 92.0 RoBERTa-DeductReasoner (2022-03). Lab reports: DeepSeek-Coder 93.3 with PAL (program-aided, uses code execution; 2023-11); Llama 2-Chat with calculator (Toolformer protocol) 82.4 (2023-07).
notes: No human baseline -> B (90). Protocol heterogeneity is the main judgement call: the paper defines an official 80/20 split, but subsequent supervised work uses 5-fold CV on a filtered subset and LLM papers evaluate assorted MAWPS sub-datasets; AB taken on the dominant supervised-MWP protocol (as in Papers-with-Code 'MAWPS' table). Chain-of-thought paper v1 (2022-01) reported MAWPS sub-datasets separately (SingleOp/SingleEq/AddSub/MultiArith), not an aggregate, so not counted. PAL / tool-integrated numbers excluded from main mode (code execution). Prior SOTA before AB: Roberta-Graph2Tree 88.7 (Patel et al., 2021). Strict event not established (no independent re-run >=90 located). Labs stopped reporting after 2023-11 (DeepSeek Coder) - after the AB event, so not 'abandoned'.

canonical_name: MBPP: Mostly Basic Python Problems (Austin et al., Google, 'Program Synthesis with Large Language Models') - incl. EvalPlus-curated 'MBPP (base tests)' variant that labs report as MBPP
metric: pass@1 (functional correctness on the original MBPP assert tests)
ab_system: OpenAI o1-mini (93.1) and o1-preview (95.5), run by EvalPlus
ab_mode: pass@1 (greedy), base (original) MBPP tests on EvalPlus MBPP set (378 tasks)
ab_source: EvalPlus leaderboard data, commits 970429d / 02023dd 2024-11-10 https://github.com/evalplus/evalplus.github.io (results.json: 'O1 Mini (Sept 2024)' mbpp 93.1; 'O1 Preview (Sept 2024)' mbpp 95.5)
score_at_release_system: 137B decoder-only LM (Google), few-shot; metric = share of problems solved by any of 80 samples (not pass@1)
n_items: 974 total; official test split 500 (task IDs 11-510); sanitized subset 427 (test 257); EvalPlus MBPP/MBPP+ set 399 (v0.1) -> 378 (v0.2) tasks
lineage: MBPP (2021-08) -> sanitized MBPP (427 hand-verified, same release) -> EvalPlus MBPP base / MBPP+ (35x more tests; Liu et al., arXiv 2305.01210, 2023-05; MBPP+ added to EvalPlus late 2023) -> MBPP Pro (self-invoking, 2024-12); sibling HumanEval (2021-07).
best_by_cutoff: 95.5 - o1-preview, EvalPlus MBPP (base tests), leaderboard 2024-11-10; QualityFlow (Claude 3.5 Sonnet v2 + LLM quality checks, no code execution) 94.2 on 'standard MBPP' (arXiv 2501.17167, 2025-01). On MBPP+ (extended tests) best 80.2 o1-preview (EvalPlus).
